The ctml windows open on a server, at most one a player, all driven from one task that runs every tick. A `WindowRenderer` opens trees here; nothing else needs to.

A tree from the `UIRegistry` is one tree, so everyone it is opened for is looking at the same elements: a callback that changes it changes it for all of them, and so does any of their cursors, since hover: and active: are kept on the elements. `buildUI` builds a tree of its own every time it is called, for a player who should have theirs.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.paper.render.CTMLWindows;
```

### `public void start()`

Starts the tick task, and undoes whatever a crash or a reload left behind.

### `public void shutdown()`

Closes every window and stops ticking.

### `public void open(Player player, String name, DOMTreeElement tree, DOMContext ctx)`

### `public void open(Player player, String name, DOMTreeElement tree, DOMContext ctx, CTMLWindow.Frame frame)`

Opens a tree in front of a player, in place of any window they already had open, under a name that `named` finds it by. Once it closes nothing here holds the tree any more, so a tree no one else keeps is gone with it.

### `public boolean close(Player player)`

Closes the player's window, and says false where they had none.
